Current assessment — 2026-10-05

Reviewed against local main 7057a8d5a2d898c1bfb528a28f3f635dda639b8b, origin/main 568ce108 (local main clean, 112 ahead/0 behind at audit; no push).

Where we are: surface/strip-raster-qualified-20260912 at 452acac8 is retained but unqualified for blanket merge. Earlier primitive-buffer preflight corrections are not total app-memory or timing proof.

Fresh context: Yes: retained candidate / native performance.

Next action: Recover the exact render-only strip candidate onto the adopted camera/render plan, independently compare joined/full pixels and original IDs, then measure public API 1350/2700/3600 work, cancellation and actual native scenes.

Evidence: docs/verification/consolidation-20261005.md; branches.json; original strip review notes.

This is a tracker/source/retained-evidence assessment, not a new experiment or test run. Existing acceptance criteria and owner decisions remain binding; dated source-state statements below are superseded where this assessment explicitly corrects them. Status, priority, assignee, claims and dependency edges are unchanged.

---

Previous scope and history (acceptance retained)

Provider prerequisite for PLS Neuro bd-01M2B710PC2X01PPK133PDPHMV. Reuse reference raster kernel and native SurfaceRenderPlan without local consumer renderer. Stream strips at global pixel coordinates with no pick buffers; explicit render-only capability receipt, memory preflight suitable for3GiB applications, cooperative cancellation and sink failure. Full-frame vs joined-strip deterministic pixel oracle on JVM+JS, real SpikeB scenes after admission. Prior spike a89b299 / PLS issue bd-01M277KNZYE5RD49J49Q9PEW8T. Current main e071e83 predates admitted paired-camera a3ee73b; integration lineage must be settled before claiming same current-app scene semantics. Source-only until serialized machine grant.
